assets.label: STARR / ProMMiS natural-history framework
assets.access_status: Published description only. Permission to adopt the protocol, its instrument licences and staff/equipment needs are not checked.
assets.description: Multi-site prospective natural history protocol for STXBP1-RD (STARR) and SYNGAP1-RD (ProMMiS): clinician-administered developmental measures, caregiver-reported measures, seizure-history reconstruction and quantitative EEG, with CHOP as prime site and data coordinating centre.
assets.owner_status: Study team documented (CHOP-led consortium). Ownership of protocol materials not established.
assets.proposed_use: A patient organization planning a natural history study reviews which framework components could inform its own protocol.
assets.documented_context: Studied in STXBP1-RD and SYNGAP1-RD cohorts only. The authors state an aim to generalize the framework to other DEEs; that extension is not demonstrated in this paper.
unverified: fit for other diseases or age ranges

public_researcher_routes.name: STARR study team via STXBP1 Foundation STARR page
ENDD Center natural history study page (CHOP / Penn)

assets.label: Medical-record seizure history reconstruction method
assets.access_status: Method described in the paper and earlier cited work. Coding manual or templates not checked.
assets.description: Month-by-month seizure type and frequency reconstructed from medical records and family interviews, seizure types coded with HPO terms and frequency mapped to the PELHS scale, with two extra levels added for very high SYNGAP1 seizure frequency.
assets.owner_status: Developed and applied by the CHOP/ENDD team per the paper; no public toolkit confirmed.
assets.proposed_use: Collect seizure history with less family burden than daily diaries when planning a natural history study.
assets.documented_context: Applied to 107 STXBP1-RD and 100 SYNGAP1-RD individuals in the preliminary analysis (preprint figures). The paper notes many seizures are uncountable, which limits seizure counts as trial endpoints.

assets.label: Quantitative EEG acquisition protocol (resting state, VEP, AEP)
assets.access_status: Acquisition settings described in the paper. Analysis pipeline code availability not checked.
assets.description: 128-channel resting EEG with visual and auditory evoked potentials every 6 months, artifact removal by automated ICA and spectral analysis.
assets.owner_status: CHOP/ENDD study team per the paper.
assets.proposed_use: Plan exploratory EEG biomarker collection alongside clinical outcome measures.
assets.documented_context: The paper calls biomarker work an initial, exploratory step; evoked-potential results are not reported there. Not a validated endpoint.

assets.label: SYNGAP1 retrospective medical-record dataset (Citizen Health, via CURE SYNGAP1)
assets.access_status: Documented access route for academic researchers: Researcher Agreement with Citizen Health plus an IRB submission. Access for a patient organization without an academic partner is not stated.
assets.description: De-identified, standardized summaries of participating patients' medical records, including genetic and EEG results; the page states data for over 100 patients with a confirmed P/LP SYNGAP1 diagnosis.
assets.owner_status: Offered by CURE SYNGAP1 and Citizen Health per their page.
assets.proposed_use: Retrospective baseline data to inform which outcomes a prospective SYNGAP1 study should measure.
assets.documented_context: Retrospective, record-derived data; not a prospective protocol. Patient count is as stated on the page, not independently checked.
unverified: data fields relevant to the chosen outcomes

assets.label: Simons Searchlight retrospective caregiver-reported data (STXBP1, SYNGAP1)
assets.access_status: Use reported in the paper only. Access conditions not checked; Simons Searchlight's own pages not reviewed.
assets.description: The paper combined existing Simons Searchlight data (STXBP1 n=67, SYNGAP1 n=39 in the preprint) with prospective RARE-X data to check feasibility of caregiver-reported measures such as the Vineland-3.
assets.owner_status: Simons Searchlight (registry operator); not confirmed from the operator's own pages.
assets.proposed_use: Comparison data for planning caregiver-reported outcome measures.
assets.documented_context: Counts come from the preprint text and may differ in the published version.

assets.label: RARE-X caregiver-reported outcome collection (used by STARR/ProMMiS)
assets.access_status: Paper states PROMs moved to RARE-X from year two once licensing agreements were finalized. Terms for another organization not checked.
assets.description: Third-party platform through which the studies administer parent-reported outcome measures; a 2024 press release describes the STXBP1 Foundation partnership with Global Genes for STARR.
assets.proposed_use: Remote collection of caregiver-reported measures for a new natural history study.
assets.documented_context: The paper reports variable caregiver completion rates despite support.
unverified: which instruments are licensed on the platform

checks.question: Is an existing natural-history framework documented?

evidence.rationale: Methods describe the STARR and ProMMiS protocols, sites and assessments.

checks.next_question: Which protocol components can be shared with our group?

checks.question: Does this paper report use in STXBP1-related disorder?

evidence.rationale: STARR is the STXBP1-RD arm; the preprint reports 164 STXBP1-RD participants enrolled.

checks.next_question: Do our proposed participants resemble the studied STXBP1 cohort (age range, severity, variant types)?

checks.question: Have permissions, materials and implementation resources been confirmed for our proposed study?

evidence.rationale: The paper says caregiver measures moved to RARE-X only once licensing agreements were finalized, and several instruments are commercially published. This shows licences matter; it does not say what our group would need.

checks.next_question: Can we access the protocol and instrument materials, and which licences, trained staff and equipment (e.g. 128-channel EEG) are required?

checks.question: Has the framework been assessed for our group's age range, travel constraints and study sites?
checks.next_question: Which components need adapting to our cohort and local study capacity? The paper notes in-person visits limit families who cannot travel.

checks.question: Is an STXBP1 patient organization documented as a partner in designing this framework?

evidence.rationale: Outcome measures were selected and reviewed with the STXBP1 Foundation (Methods).
Foundation page states it funds STARR.

checks.next_question: Would the STXBP1 Foundation share what they learned from co-designing STARR?

checks.question: Is STARR currently enrolling?

evidence.rationale: The undated foundation page says all five listed sites are enrolling; the page date is unknown, so current status needs confirmation.

checks.next_question: Is STARR enrolling now, and at which sites?

checks.question: Has responsiveness to treatment been established by this paper?

evidence.rationale: Authors say longitudinal data are still needed, and countable seizures were present in only about a quarter of the STXBP1 cohort up to age 10.

checks.next_question: What additional validation is needed before selecting a treatment-trial endpoint?
